gates.evidence: The proposed surface is the Attachment and Mode Sheet (s27), which is a utility screen for photo processing, entirely SFW and age-appropriate.
The reward is in-app photo analysis credits, which are non-transferable and not cash-like. There is no incentive for clicks, installs, or ratings.
The offer uses benefit-driven language ('Get Free Photo Credits') and includes a clear, neutral 'No Thanks' option, avoiding dark patterns.
The offer is an opt-in invitation card with explicit 'Play Now' and 'No Thanks' buttons, as stated in the storyboard.
The offer specifies the reward ('3 bonus photo analysis credits') and the required action ('Play a quick game with Luzia').
The offer includes a 'No Thanks' option, and declining allows the user to continue using the app at the pre-offer state.
The trigger occurs on the Attachment and Mode Sheet (s27), which is a pre-generation or utility state, not a streaming AI chat response.
The proposal states it is 'Gated strictly to non-subscribers'.

scores.evidence: The trigger occurs exactly when a non-subscriber hits their quota limit while attempting an action, which is the high-intent moment of need.
The proposal fits natively into the existing Attachment and Mode Sheet flow, using the character Luzia as a Game Partner in-world.
The design is gated strictly to non-subscribers, uses a temporary consumable resource (bonus credits), and implements a conservative daily cap of 3.
Code-computed economics reveal a cost to serve ($0.0250/view) that significantly exceeds the net revenue per view ($0.0063/view), making the current 3-credit grant unsustainable.
Photo analysis and image generation are part of the core Luzia loop, providing frequent and broad reach for the offer.
The proposal uses existing Simula units (SIM-RWD), existing screens, and clear resource definitions, minimizing technical overhead.
Uses app-specific nouns including Luzia, 'Attachment and Mode Sheet' (s27), and 'Photo Analysis Credits' (r3).
Implements an explicit daily cap of 3 and a 15-minute cooldown, which prevents nagging and fatigue.
Defines primary metrics (Rewarded ARPDAU), guardrails (subscription conversion, retention), and a user-level holdout experiment.

requiredChanges: Reduce the reward grant size from 3 credits to 1 credit per view, or implement a 2-view bundle requirement to align COGS with net revenue.
Perform an additional unit-economic review after adjusting the reward size to ensure the cost to serve remains within the 60% threshold of net revenue per view.
parsed.topConcern: The unit economics are currently negative, as granting 3 photo credits per view costs significantly more ($0.0250) than the net revenue generated per view ($0.0063).
